summary: 120-foot Wisconsin standard tower built in 1949 near Rhinelander; the state decommissioned its lookouts in 2015 and the tower is now privately owned.

facts.design: Wisconsin Standard Ladder Protected design with an external, cage-protected ladder
facts.agency: Private owner (formerly Wisconsin Department of Natural Resources)

access.note: Now under private ownership. The register documents no public access; a WJFW article describes its author and a friend climbing the tower, with no date or permission stated.

events.note: Built 1949 per NHLR; a May 24, 1949 Rhinelander Daily News report, reprinted by Central US Lookouts, gave a planned completion by the end of June
Staffed intermittently during spring fire season until 2015, when Wisconsin decommissioned its lookout network
Registered April 3, 2018; nominated by Tyler Bormann; NHLR US 1269, WI 50

notes_for_editor: Built 1949 and the 2015 decommissioning are well supported. Sale date and buyer are unknown. The register says the tower was built for a standard design by the Wisconsin Conservation Commission; the 1949 newspaper header names the Wisconsin Department of Conservation, so the builder agency is not settled. The register photo captions disagree with their file names (caption 'August 1952 photo' vs file 'hodag_tower_april_30_1952'); both NHLR photos are already in the record. A WJFW article describes its author and a friend climbing the tower, with no date or permission stated. The story cites it for that account; it is not evidence of public access. The record's 36.6 m matches the register's 120 feet; the register does not say whether that is to the cab floor.
